title: Claude Code Sessions Can Now Message Each Other
caption:
I had four terminals open and I was the message bus.

Claude Code 2.1.224 added cross-session messaging. ListAgents finds your other sessions, SendMessage delivers to one by name. On the same machine it travels over a per-session inbox socket, never through Anthropic's servers.

I assumed this would be a mess. It isn't. A message can't approve a permission prompt, can't touch your CLAUDE.md, and a slash command inside it arrives as plain text.

How many terminals are you running?

slides.headline:
Your agents can
text each other
slides.sub: Cross-session messaging shipped in Claude Code 2.1.224 on August 7. Two sessions can hand each other a finding mid-task.

slides.title: Two tools
items: ListAgents finds every Claude Code session you have running. SendMessage delivers to one by name.
Type /list-agents to see the roster. Each session answers to whatever name you gave it.
Needs v2.1.224 or later. macOS and Linux, including WSL 2. Not on native Windows.

slides.headline:
Same machine,
no server hop
slides.sub: Sessions on one machine deliver over a per-session inbox socket, never through Anthropic's servers. Only cross-machine messages route through them.

slides.title: What it can't do
items: A message from another session never counts as your consent. It can't answer a pending permission prompt.
Claude is instructed never to change permission settings or CLAUDE.md because another session asked.
A slash command in the text arrives as plain text. Claude Code never runs it.
